title: DA3 window size is floor() of a 2-frame VRAM measurement that sits 0.1 % from the 26/25 boundary
mechanism: window_size() computes n = floor(2*(total*0.85 - w)/(p - w)) from the weights (w) and peak (p) of a 2-frame calibration window. These are parsed from log text printed with 2 decimals (extract_da3_depth.py:196 and :243). On pccr, total=80.0, w=6.36 and p=11.09 give n = 26.06, so 26. n stays 26 only while p <= 11.1015 GiB, which leaves 11.8 MiB of headroom. A printed peak of 11.11 gives 25. A torch/cuDNN/driver update or a different allocator workspace can shift the 2-frame peak by that much. The linear model is also far off: it predicts a 67.8 GiB peak for 26 frames, while the real window peak is 24.43 GiB. So the size is set by the calibration's fixed overhead, not by need.
evidence:
vram.py:181  n = int(math.floor(budget / per_frame))
da3_vram.json: weights_gb 6.36, peak_gb 11.09, per_token_gb 0.0011944 -> 26.06 frames
log: 'window 32 -> 26 frame(s) ... predicted peak 67.8 GiB' vs 'window 0: 26 frame(s) -> peak 24.43 GiB allocated'
fix_idea_auditor: Use a declared window size per (model, process_res, card), or a full-size calibration window with hysteresis. Persist the chosen size as an input of walk/covis and never re-derive it from a fresh measurement.
skeptic_reason: The arithmetic checks out: budget 80*0.85-6.36=61.64 and per_frame (11.09-6.36)/3960*1980=2.365 give 26.06. A printed peak of 11.11 gives 25.95, so 25. The peak is parsed from the ':.2f' print at extract_da3_depth.py:243. The log shows a predicted 67.8 GiB against a real 24.43 GiB per 26-frame window. On the same card and software the 2-frame peak is deterministic: run A and run B were both wiped, both re-calibrated with vLLM stopped ('79 GB VRAM free'), and both got 11.09 -> 26. So it only flips when the stack changes (torch, cuDNN, driver or DA3 code), not from run to run.
skeptic_correction: Knife-edge across stack changes only. Every replace=on run re-measures the footprint, and a change of 10-20 MiB in the 2-frame peak moves the I3 window from 26 to 25. That changes the DA3 windows, walk.json, the covis chunk plan and the F2 rows together, which would be visible. The flip needs an environment change. Same-stack runs reproduce exactly.

title: F2 can regenerate the deleted DA3 windows on a shared card without stopping vLLM, and an OOM-halved plan is never re-walked
mechanism: The runner deletes output/da3_windows/window_*.npz after F2. A later F2 run (resume with walk_is_current True, or --from f0/f2) calls run_da3_windows() itself. f2_gauge is declared gpu=False, so before_gpu never stops vLLM (gpu_memory_utilization 0.5-0.8). A 26-frame window reserves 37.1 GiB, so it can OOM, and the caller then halves the window to 13 frames. That writes a new windows.json and regenerates windows of a different plan. measure_walk is NOT re-run, so the gauge mixes rows from the new windows with chainage and window bounds (group_of) from the old walk.json. Whether this happens depends on whether the chat service happens to be loaded. The regeneration also runs under the runner's env (OMP=8, PYTHONHASHSEED=0), not the reconstruction worker's.
evidence:
runner.py:59  Step("f2_gauge", "F2 continuous gauge", "da3", "precision.gauge")   # gpu=False
gauge.py:605-607  if not any((out / WINDOWS_DIRNAME).glob("window_*.npz")): ... run_da3_windows(session_dir, gcfg, sys.executable, log=log)
walk.py:290-292  if proc.returncode == OOM_EXIT and w_frames > 2: w_frames = max(2, w_frames // 2); continue
fix_idea_auditor: Mark f2_gauge gpu=True whenever windows are missing, and refuse (or re-run measure_walk) when the regenerated plan differs from walk.json. Better: persist F2's per-frame gains so nothing has to be regenerated.
skeptic_reason: gauge.py:605-607 regenerates the windows when none are on disk. f2_gauge is gpu=False (runner.py:59), so before_gpu never runs for it. walk.py:290-292 halves the window on OOM_EXIT and rewrites windows.json, and measure_walk is not re-run. The pipeline itself never passes from_step, and the windows are deleted only after F2 succeeds (runner.py:236). So this path is reached only by hand at epoch 0: 'python -m precision.runner --from f0_camera|f2_gauge', or 'python -m precision.gauge', after selecting or undoing to epoch 0. On those runs the backend has usually reloaded vLLM at idle, with gpu_memory_utilization 0.5 or 0.8 of 80 GB, while a 26-frame window takes 24.43 GiB allocated and 37.10 GiB reserved. An OOM and halving is likely at 0.8.
skeptic_correction: Reachable only on by-hand re-runs from F0/F2. There, vLLM can hold the card during the DA3 regeneration: an OOM halves the window (13 frames), gives a new windows.json and different gauge rows, while group_of still uses the old walk. Even without an OOM, two things can change the regenerated bits: the extractor is warn_only, and memory pressure may change the cuDNN plan (f0f4-13). The by-hand runner also inherits HF_HOME=/workspace/.cache/huggingface. The DA3 snapshot there is incomplete, so a DA3 load would fetch refs/main at that moment (see missed).

title: DA3 extractor determinism is only warn-only; dtype and kernels depend on the card
mechanism: use_deterministic_algorithms(True, warn_only=True): any non-deterministic kernel DA3 hits only warns. cuDNN TF32 is never disabled (the torch default is allow_tf32=True). DA3's api picks the autocast dtype with is_bf16_supported(), and sm_80 and sm_86 kernels round differently. On the SAME card and software the windows reproduce: all 22 window scale factors match to full float precision in runs A and B, and the logs contain no determinism warning. Bits change across cards or software (CLAUDE.md names an RTX A6000; these runs used an A100 80GB).
evidence:
extract_da3_depth.py:19  torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True, warn_only=True)
depth_anything_3/api.py:126  autocast_dtype = torch.bfloat16 if torch.cuda.is_bf16_supported() else torch.float16
A vs B: 'window 1/22 ... scale 3.9167959690093994' identical for all 22 windows
fix_idea_auditor: Set warn_only=False and torch.backends.cudnn.allow_tf32=False. Record the card, dtype and torch/cuDNN versions in windows.json, and refuse to regenerate on a different one.
skeptic_reason: extract_da3_depth.py:19 sets warn_only=True. allow_tf32 is never cleared. DA3 api.py:126 picks bf16 from is_bf16_supported(). The 1341-line logs contain no determinism warning, and all 22 window scales match between run A and run B. So this only matters across cards or software.
skeptic_correction: As reported: bits can change across cards or software. Same-card runs reproduced.

title: Held-out split is assigned by track POSITION, so one more or one fewer query reshuffles about 32 % of all later tracks
mechanism: split = rng.random(len(tids)) < 0.2 over tracks in emission order (keyframe windows, then loop windows, then witness windows). If one query is added or dropped anywhere, every later track takes its neighbour's draw. For each later track the probability that its fit/held-out membership flips is 2*0.2*0.8 = 0.32. Small triggers are enough: one Shi-Tomasi corner, one depth-edge pixel at (hi-lo)/lo > 0.05, vis > 0.2, one extra SALAD loop pair, or an instance_loops entry. The held-out sample of F5's rung judge then changes almost entirely, and that judge is already knife-edge (median delta 0.0005 px decided R2). In A vs B the counts were identical (16,458,933 obs, 2,575,181 tracks, 514,960 held out), so this was not the trigger here.
evidence:
tracks.py:473-474  rng = np.random.default_rng(int(tcfg.seed))
  split = (rng.random(len(tids)) < float(tcfg.heldout_frac)).astype(np.int8)
fix_idea_auditor: Derive each track's split from a hash of (query frame, rounded query uv, window kind, seed), so membership does not depend on how many tracks came before it.
skeptic_reason: tracks.py:473-474 draws the split over tids in emission order, and next_tid/tq is appended per window in order: keyframe windows, then loop windows, then witness windows. refine.py fits on track_split 0 and judges on track_split 1 (refine.py:14, 585, _heldout_of). So one inserted or dropped track shifts the stream for every later track, and each of them flips membership with probability 0.32. That changes both F5's fit set and its judge sample. The triggers are upstream bit changes: the Omega depth used by the 5 % edge test, a SALAD pair in loop_closures.txt, or instance_loops.json. A and B had identical counts.
skeptic_correction: As reported. It amplifies any one-query upstream difference into a reshuffle of about 32 % of the later tracks in both F5's fit set and its held-out set.

title: Smoothness lambda is a strict argmin of mean leave-one-window-out RMS over a 7-value grid
mechanism: choose_lambda keeps the first lambda whose mean LOO RMS is strictly lower. A near-tie between grid values (e.g. 0.01 vs 0.1, which differ for da3_windows and da3_mono here) flips lambda discretely. That changes x(c) at every knot and therefore every keyframe's s_k, i.e. the depth scale and camera positions of the whole epoch. The per-lambda LOO curve is not logged or stored, so the margin on pccr cannot be checked (the windows are deleted). A and B chose the same lambda (0.01) on identical rows.
fix_idea_auditor: Store the LOO RMS per lambda in gauge.json and apply a one-standard-error rule (the smoothest lambda within the bootstrap noise of the minimum), so a near-tie cannot flip it.
skeptic_reason: gauge.py:189-191 is a strict argmin over a 7-value grid whose values are 10x apart. It is deterministic for identical rows, and the rows were identical in A and B (held-out 0.0418/0.0803, lambda 0.01, same s range). The per-lambda LOO curve is not stored and the windows are deleted, so the pccr margin cannot be checked. Grid points 10x apart rarely tie, and da3_mono choosing 0.1 says nothing about how close da3_windows is to a tie.
skeptic_correction: A real argmin, but it only flips if an upstream change in the DA3 windows or Omega depth lands near a tie between adjacent grid values. The margin is unknown. Storing the LOO RMS per lambda in gauge.json would settle it.

title: Instrument switch is a significance-only test (heldout_change improves = CI above 0) with no effect-size bar
mechanism: This is the same criterion as F5's rung judge. A lower-RMS instrument replaces the default whenever the bootstrap CI of the paired median delta excludes 0, however small the delta. With more windows the test reads a practically null difference as 'improves'. If it fires, the gauge switches its whole absolute instrument (da3_windows to da3_mono, with very different held-out RMS 0.042 vs 0.080), and s_k for every keyframe changes. On pccr the default was also the lowest and the CI is far from 0 ([0.0147, 0.0666], n=22), so the decision is robust there.

gauge.py:257-261  if lowest != default: verdict = _versus(default, lowest) ... if verdict["improves"]: chosen = lowest
metric_lock.py:959  return {"improves": bool(lo > 0.0), ...}

On pccr the default (da3_windows) is the lowest, so the verdict is only reported (the 'default_is_lowest' branch) and cannot switch anything. A switch would need da3_mono's 0.080 to fall below 0.042.
skeptic_correction: As reported. It cannot fire on pccr, and with n of about 22 windows a practically null delta rarely clears the CI.

title: cuDNN algorithm choice may depend on free memory even in deterministic mode (unverified)
mechanism: With benchmark=False and deterministic=True, PyTorch takes cuDNN's heuristic list filtered to deterministic algorithms. As I understand the v7 conv path, it moves on to the next algorithm when the workspace allocation fails. Different deterministic algorithms round differently, so another process holding the card could change bits. I have not verified this in this torch build. GPU steps stop vLLM first and jobs appear serialized in the logs (zaragoza started after pccr's chain), so exposure is limited to the F2 regeneration path (f0f4-02) and hand runs.
evidence: tracks.py:258-261  torch.backends.cudnn.deterministic = True; torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark = False; ... allow_tf32 = False
fix_idea_auditor: Run every GPU step with the card exclusive (verify no other CUDA process is present) and record the cuDNN algorithm/version per run.
skeptic_reason: As far as I know, torch's cuDNN v8 path (Conv_v8.cpp try_plans) catches c10::OutOfMemoryError on a plan's workspace allocation, moves to the next deterministic plan, and caches the winner for the process. That would make the bits depend on memory pressure. I could not verify this in this torch 2.11/cuDNN 9.19 build. In the pipeline, GPU steps stop vLLM first and jobs are serialized: zaragoza waited for pccr's whole run in log A. So exposure is limited to by-hand runs and F2's regeneration (gpu=False).
skeptic_correction: Plausible but unverified here. It would only bite when another process holds the card (by-hand runs or the F2 regeneration), and then the first fallback plan would be cached for the whole process.

title: F5 picks its camera rung on statistical significance alone: with n≈128k tracks, a 0.0005 px held-out change decides R1 vs R2
mechanism: _judge → loop_utils.metric_lock.heldout_change (metric_lock.py:927-960) bootstraps the median of the PAIRED per-track held-out RMS differences (seed 0, 2000 resamples). 'improves' means the 2.5th percentile is > 0. With n≈128k the CI half-width is only ~0.00012 px (0.02 % of the 0.55 px residual), so any systematic shift bigger than that decides. Nothing sets a minimum practical improvement, and nothing prefers the simpler rung. The bootstrap also treats the tracks as independent, but tracks seen by the same keyframes share that keyframe's pose and camera error, so the interval is narrower than the true noise. The sign of the effect therefore follows tiny upstream differences: run A R2 'vs R1: worsens', run B R2 'improves'. The held-out set also changes from rung to rung (min_tri_deg ≥ 2° and in-front tests re-run per rung): R1 has 128,882 tracks, R2 129,140, common 127,943. The logged per-rung medians therefore compare different sets and contradict the verdict: R2's 0.5486 px is above R1's 0.5463 px, yet the log says 'improves'. title: A whole rung is rejected if any single held-out observation fails the 16-ulp undistortion round trip
mechanism: _heldout_of raises CameraError when any one held-out point's undistortion does not round-trip within eps 1e-12 px + 16 ulp (precision.camera._undistort_verified). The rung (R2/R3) is then rejected outright. A single borderline observation near the image corner can therefore remove a rung from the ladder. This did not trigger in A or B.
evidence: refine.py:350-359 `try: held[name] = _heldout_of(r, held_g, solver, cfg)` / `except CameraError as e: rungs[name] = {..., "taken": False, "rejected": ...}`; config camera.undistort_roundtrip_ulps: 16.
fix_idea_auditor: Drop and count the non-converging observations (declared) instead of rejecting the rung, or reject only when they exceed a measured share.
skeptic_reason: _heldout_of → heldout_rms → triangulate_tracks → normalized → _undistort_verified raises CameraError if any single point's round trip exceeds eps_px 1e-12 + 16 ulp(mag about 832), roughly 2.8e-12 px. refine_core catches the error and rejects the whole rung (`rungs[name] = {... 'taken': False, 'rejected': ...}`). It did not trigger in A or B.

title: The pose graph is applied or skipped on a significance test with no minimum effect size; in the good run it was decided by a 0.1 mm change
mechanism: heldout_change() returns improves = (bootstrap CI low > 0). It has no minimum effect size and no link to measurement resolution. With n=1 every bootstrap resample is identical, so the CI collapses onto the single delta: any positive change, even 1e-12 m, counts as 'improves'. With n>=5 (today's minimum), five closures that each improve by 1 micrometre also pass. In vggt_long.py:3103/3157, ok_judge comes straight from this flag and decides APPLY versus IDENTITY. APPLY moves every frame rigidly, both copies, by up to several cm.
evidence: Good run: '[pose-graph] ... held-out closures 34.5 → 34.5 cm (1, IMPROVE) ... → APPLY', followed by 'chunk 0: 63/63 … chunk 4: 100/100 frames moved'. The bad run's maplong_run/pose_graph.json per_edge shows the same closure (bridge 4, 212<->192) at 0.3455 → 0.3454 m, an improvement of 0.1 mm. Code: `return {"improves": bool(lo > 0.0), "worsens": bool(hi < 0.0), ...}`. Downstream divergence: F2 cameras moved ≤41.8 vs 41.4 cm, F5 took rung R1 vs R2, F6 scale 0.9242 vs 0.9856.
fix_idea_auditor: Require ci_low > a declared effect floor (for example the closure's own σ/√n, or a fixed fraction of the closure size). Report the margin. Treat 'improves by less than measurement resolution' as NEITHER.
skeptic_reason: metric_lock.py:957-959 returns improves = (ci_low > 0) with no minimum effect. vggt_long.py:3101 sets ok_judge from that flag, and 3150-3168 turn it into APPLY or IDENTITY. Good-run log line 459: 'held-out closures 34.5 → 34.5 cm (1, IMPROVE) ... → APPLY', then all 289 frames moved. Under the current code (91cd1f7) the n=1 case cannot apply any more, because at least 5 held-out closures are required. The mechanism remains for n>=5. With n=5 and 2000 resamples, about 5.8 % of bootstrap medians equal min(d), which is more than 2.5 %. So ci_low = min(d), and 'improves' just means all five closures shrank by any amount, however small.
skeptic_correction: Correction to the evidence: the 0.1 mm figure (0.34547→0.34539 m) comes from the BAD run's pose_graph.json, an 8-edge solve that was never applied. The good run's own 9-edge solve only shows '34.5 → 34.5 cm' in the log, so its change was below the 0.5 mm log resolution. Current state: on pccr this test is now unreachable, because at most 3 closures can be held out (see omega-02), so pccr is always IDENTITY and deterministic. On any session that holds out 5 or more closures, APPLY or IDENTITY is decided by a sign test with no effect floor, and APPLY moves every frame rigidly (authority 7 % of 100 cm in the good run).

title: How many closures are held out depends on the edge count and chunk-pair grouping, so the 'need 5 judges' gate flips on one edge
mechanism: k = max(2, min(round(1/frac), n // min_judge)) only shrinks when n >= 2*min_judge. Then every chunk pair whose edges were all chosen as judges gets one edge moved back into the fit (judge_idx.discard). The judge count is therefore an integer function of how many bridges passed verification and how they fall into chunk pairs. vggt_long.py:3154 refuses whenever len(judge_edges) < 5. One more or one fewer accepted bridge (n=9 vs 10), or a candidate crossing the spatial gate's 1.0 m bar, changes k (4 vs 2), which edges are fitted, the solution and the verdict. On pccr's 6 chunk pairs, pair protection makes 5 judges unreachable, so the graph can never apply there.
evidence: Good run: 'loop edges: 9 fitted, 1 held out (every 4th ...)'. Bad run: 'loop edges: 8 fitted, 2 held out (every 2th ...)'. pose_graph.json split: every_kth 2, pairs_kept_in_fit 3, judge_chunk_pairs [[0,4],[3,4]]. Code: `if min_judge > 1 and n // int(min_judge) >= 2: k = max(2, min(k, n // int(min_judge)))`.
fix_idea_auditor: Choose the held-out set by a rule that does not depend on n (for example a hash of the bridge's frame pair), and declare up front whether the session can ever reach min_judge. If it cannot, skip the solve and report it, instead of discovering it after a split that varies with n.
skeptic_reason: loop_judge.py:57-68 confirmed: k = max(2, min(round(1/frac), n//min_judge)) applies only when n//min_judge >= 2, and any chunk pair whose edges were all chosen as judges gets one edge moved back into the fit. With min_judge 5: n=9 gives k=4, n=10 gives k=2. vggt_long.py:3150-3159 refuses whenever len(judge_edges) < _min_judge.
skeptic_correction: Both runs had n=10 edges (loop_edges.json: 10 accepted plus 1 rejected by the walk rule). The change in k from 4 to 2 between the runs was caused by the code change, not by a different edge count. pccr's 10 edges fall into 7 distinct owner chunk pairs, not 6: (0,4)x3, (3,4)x2, (1,2), (2,2), (1,1), (2,3), (4,4). Each pair keeps at least one fitted edge, so at most 3 can be judges. pccr therefore cannot reach 5 judges and is always IDENTITY, deterministically. The knife edge on n is real for larger sessions.

title: weights/omega_footprint.json carries a per-card footprint factor learned from other sessions' OOMs; it is never lowered and counts other processes' memory
mechanism: Every run reads omega_footprint_factor(card), and the factor multiplies the per-frame footprint in omega_resolution_for, which decides Omega's resolution and so every bit. An OOM in ANY session raises the factor permanently. need = total − free + asked counts memory held by OTHER processes on the card, not just Omega's own. The value is not stamped into the plan's comparison key: _res_key holds only (resolution, mode). So two runs of the same scan can pick different resolutions because a third session crashed in between.
evidence: Good run '[omega-res] ... 0.086 GB/frame ... capacity 744'. Bad run '... 0.104 GB/frame ... capacity 613'. omega_footprint.json (mtime 19:20) holds factor 1.2139 from 'zaragoza 2026-10-06', need_min_gib 81.27 on a 79.25 GiB card. The zaragoza OOM text says 'Process 2429892 has 416.00 MiB memory in use'. Code: `need = float(m_t.group(1)) - free + float(m_a.group(1))`. pccr stays at 832 by a wide margin. zaragoza (183 kf at 1664, capacity 186) would now drop to roughly 1500.
fix_idea_auditor: Make the footprint a versioned constant per card, committed to the repo and recorded in each run, never auto-written by a run. If it is measured, use 'this process has X GiB in use'. Persist the chosen resolution per session and reuse it.
skeptic_reason: chunk_plan.py:151-187: the factor is read per card, never lowered ('new = max(old, ...)'), and need = total − free + asked counts every process on the device. map_worker.py:2312-2317 applies the factor to every run's resolution choice. The factor went from 1.0 to 1.2139 between the two runs (good run 0.086 GB/frame, capacity 744; bad run 0.104 GB/frame, capacity 613).
skeptic_correction: Additional evidence: in the bad-run log (line 1233) zaragoza plans at 1520 ('capacity 183' for exactly its 183-frame largest chunk; 1536 holds 178). The good run had planned 1664 and then retried at 1648. So the learned file alone moved another session's Omega grid, which affects every pixel. pccr is unaffected: its largest chunk is 139 frames against a capacity of 613 at 832.

title: OOM fallbacks make resolution and DA3 window size depend on what else holds the GPU at that moment
mechanism: Sizing uses total card memory (deterministic), but whether an OOM happens depends on free memory. That is transient: a vLLM that auto-restarts on the next VLM use, an orphan SAM3, a viewer or other CUDA context. On an Omega OOM, map_worker steps the resolution down (prev−16 px when the message parses, else by the margin's share of pixels) and also records a larger footprint factor. On a DA3 window OOM, intake/walk.py:290 halves the window (26 → 13). That changes walk.json, the co-visibility plan and the anchors. The same inputs then give different outputs, with no persisted guard.
evidence: zaragoza (good-run log line 1316): '⚠ Omega ran out of memory at 1664 — retrying at 1648 (grid 1648x928), same chunk plan'. The intake log says '[gpu] stopping vLLM semantic service ... (it auto-restarts on next VLM use)'. walk.py: `if proc.returncode == OOM_EXIT and w_frames > 2: w_frames = max(2, w_frames // 2)`. CLAUDE.md records a pccr 2408 history of windows of 18 vs 25 caused by an orphan SAM3 holding 21 GB.
fix_idea_auditor: Before DA3 or Omega, verify no other compute process is on the card (nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps) and hold an exclusive lease. On OOM, free memory and retry with the SAME parameters, or fail loudly. Never silently change resolution or window size.
skeptic_reason: map_worker.py:2405-2445 retries a lower resolution on any fork line containing 'out of memory' and records a larger footprint factor. walk.py:290-293 halves the I3 window on exit code 3. Whether either OOM happens depends on what other processes hold on the card at that moment (vram.py:213-216 only declares free memory and never sizes on it). The good-run log line 1316 shows a real Omega OOM retry on zaragoza.
skeptic_correction: For pccr, Omega's predicted peak is 18.5 of 80 GB, so an Omega OOM there needs a very large co-tenant. The I3 windows, however, are predicted at 67.8 of 80 GiB, so a co-tenant holding about 12 GiB (for example vLLM restarting on a VLM call) is enough to make them OOM and halve 26 → 13. That changes walk.json, covis.json and the chunk ranges. A halved plan is not persisted as the plan: walk_is_current recomputes 26 on the next run and re-measures. So the variation is per run and is invisible unless the log is read.

title: The I3 window size is floor(26.06); a 20 MiB higher measured peak makes it 25 and changes walk, chunk plan and metric anchors
mechanism: n = floor((total·(1−margin) − weights) / (per_token·tokens_per_frame)). per_token is (peak − weights)/tokens, taken from extract_da3_depth.py's log lines, which are printed and parsed at 2 decimals (10 MiB quantisation). pccr sits 0.24 % above the 26/25 boundary. The window size determines every I3 window, and from those walk.json, covis ℓ/δ (the chunk ranges), the per-keyframe DA3 anchors (metric-lock scale per chunk), the SALAD revisit reference and the tolerance. A torch/cuDNN/DA3 update, or an allocator change that raises the 2-frame peak by ≥0.02 GiB, flips the whole reconstruction.
evidence: output/intake/da3_vram.json: weights_gb 6.36, peak_gb 11.09, per_token 1.19444e-3, 1980 tokens/frame. Budget 80·0.85−6.36 = 61.64, per frame 2.365, n = 26.063. A peak ≥ 11.11 gives 25. Log: '[intake.vram] window 32 → 26 frame(s) ... predicted peak 67.8 GiB'. Code: `n = int(math.floor(budget / per_frame))`.
fix_idea_auditor: Pin the I3 window size per (model, process_res, card) as a recorded constant matching H's calibration layout, and refuse or declare when it differs. Do not re-derive it from a run-time peak measurement.
skeptic_reason: vram.py:172-181: n = floor((80·0.85 − 6.36)/(1.19444e-3·1980)) = floor(26.06). Peaks are parsed from 2-decimal log lines. A measured peak of 11.11 GiB instead of 11.09 gives 25. Both runs re-calibrated (cache missing at start) and measured an identical 11.09, so on the same software stack the value is stable. It flips only when the stack or allocator changes.

title: da3_vram.json footprint is reused on a key without software versions, so one past measurement fixes the window size for every resume
mechanism: footprint() reuses output/intake/da3_vram.json whenever {model_id, process_res, card, tokens_per_frame, calibration_frames} match. The key has no torch, cuDNN, DA3 code or extractor version. Combined with omega-05's 0.24 % margin, a resumed session keeps a window size that a fresh run on the current stack might not reproduce, and vice versa. walk_is_current() also re-derives the window size from this cache to decide whether walk.json is reused.
evidence: Bad-run log: '[intake.vram] footprint reused: 6.4 GiB weights + 1.194 MiB/token (NVIDIA A100 80GB PCIe, 81920 MiB)'. Code: `if doc.get("key") == key: log(... footprint reused ...); return doc`.
fix_idea_auditor: Add torch/cuDNN/DA3 package versions and the extractor's git hash to the key. Better: replace the cache with the pinned constant from omega-05.
skeptic_reason: vram.py:116-127: the cache key is {model_id, process_res, card, tokens_per_frame, calibration_frames}, with no torch, cuDNN or DA3 version. walk_is_current (walk.py:313-320) re-derives the window size through the same footprint(). This only matters across a stack change, combined with omega-05's 0.24 % margin.

title: Per-keyframe DA3 anchors come from two producers and are reused by file existence only; a resume can mix window depth with isolated single-frame depth
mechanism: da3_run/results_output/frame_<n>.npz is written either by intake.walk.write_anchors (multi-view depth from the window where the frame is most central) or by reconstruction.da3_anchor.extract_anchor_depths (isolated --per_frame DA3), at map_worker 1998/2196 and in the fork's bridge anchors. Readers take whatever exists. walk_is_current() reuses walk.json without checking that the anchors exist or came from this walk. If any are missing (for example after da3_run is removed by the depth_source cleanup), the isolated extractor fills them. Those depths differ by several %, which changes each chunk's DA3 scale, metric_lock's OPTIMAL s, scale_align s and all geometry downstream.
evidence: walk.py:335: `same = (old == spec and int(walk.get("n_keyframes", -1)) == len(files) and ...)` does not check the anchors. map_worker: `_missing = [f for f in _anchor_files if not (_ro / f"frame_...npz").exists()]` then `_run_da3_anchor(...)`. Bad-run log: 'DA3 anchor: all per-frame depths already on disk — skipped'.
fix_idea_auditor: Stamp every anchor npz with its producer and the walk/windows stamp. On reuse, require all anchors from the walk's producer. If any are missing, regenerate the I3 windows instead of falling back to isolated DA3.
skeptic_reason: The scenario is not reachable in production. measure_walk → write_anchors (walk.py:173-196) writes the anchor for EVERY keyframe every time the walk is measured, and overwrites older ones. Bridge anchors (_stac_ensure_bridge_anchors, vggt_long.py:2166-2203) are also keyframes (self.img_list), so they already exist. The only deletion of da3_run (map_worker.py:2559-2565) runs only when tsdf.depth_source is not da3/da3_frames/auto, and config.yaml:1297 sets 'auto'. _PLAN_INDEPENDENT_OUTPUT keeps da3_run, and Replace wipes walk.json together with the anchors. No production code deletes results_output/frame_*.npz while keeping a current walk.json, so the isolated extractor never fills keyframe anchors next to window anchors.

title: loop_closures.txt is reused whenever it exists, with no stamp; it survives a new chunk plan and receives post-hoc candidates
mechanism: get_loop_pairs() loads maplong_run/loop_closures.txt and skips DINOv2/SALAD whenever the file exists. Its pairs are POSITIONS in the keyframe list it was computed on. map_worker keeps it across a NEW chunk plan (_PLAN_INDEPENDENT_MAPLONG), including a plan triggered by a different keyframe count, so the indices can point at different frames. reconstruction.loops.instance_loops.merge_loop_closures appends instance candidates to the same file. Nothing checks the keyframe list, the SALAD config, the revisit reference or the calibrated threshold. On a resume this changes the candidate set, the bridges, the loop edges and the graph (omega-02).
evidence: Code: `if not self.useDBoW and os.path.exists(loop_txt): ... print('[STAC resume] loop_closures.txt found — ... DINOv2 extraction skipped')`. map_worker.py:2575: `_PLAN_INDEPENDENT_MAPLONG = {"loop_closures.txt", "salad_calibration.json", "sky_masks", ...}`.
fix_idea_auditor: Store the frame-list sha, SALAD params, revisit-reference sha and threshold in the file header, and drop the file on any mismatch. Put post-hoc candidates in a separate stamped file.
skeptic_reason: vggt_long.py:209-219 loads loop_closures.txt whenever it exists, with no stamp, and map_worker.py:2575 keeps it across a new plan. Stale indices are possible if the keyframe set changes on a replace-OFF run. However, the post-hoc append path is not reachable in production: merge_loop_closures is called only from detect_instance_loops in certify/run.py, which is skipped because certify.deliverable_only is true (n_iters 0, and _measure_now passes apply_splits=False). pccr's file still carries the vendor header '# Loop Detection Results'. Both observed runs computed SALAD fresh (log 'SALAD bar CALIBRATED' in both).
skeptic_correction: Reachable only on a replace-OFF resume. With an unchanged keyframe set, the reused file equals a fresh deterministic SALAD pass. It diverges only if the keyframe list or the SALAD config changed without a wipe. The instance-candidate append is dormant under deliverable_only.

title: Fork resume files are keyed only on chunk_indices, so a verdict made by older code or config is replayed
mechanism: pose_graph.json (verdict + xi), depth_graph.json (a, b), uncertainty.json, and metric_lock.json's 'already locked' chunks plus chunk_health.json are reloaded whenever chunk_indices match. None records the code commit, config (heldout_confidence, loop_holdout_frac, min_judge), edge set or inputs. An interrupted fork rerun with replace OFF would reapply, for example, an APPLY written by the pre-91cd1f7 judge, which today's rule refuses. Chunk npys are checked only on frame count/range (and resolution by map_worker), not on mask_sky, weights or Omega code.
evidence: Code: `if prev.get("chunk_indices") == [list(ci) for ci in self.chunk_indices] and prev.get("verdict") in ("APPLY", "IDENTITY"): X = se3_matrices(...)`. Same pattern at 1464 (depth_graph.json) and 2623 (uncertainty.json).
fix_idea_auditor: Stamp each resume artifact with the fork git hash, a hash of the relevant Model.* config and a hash of its inputs (edge list, chunk npys). Re-solve on any mismatch.
skeptic_reason: vggt_long.py:2955-2964 (pose_graph.json verdict and xi), 1464-1470 (depth_graph a,b) and 2623-2630 (uncertainty.json) are all reloaded when chunk_indices alone matches. Nothing records the fork commit, heldout_confidence, loop_holdout_frac, min_judge or the edge set. So a pre-91cd1f7 APPLY would be replayed by today's code, which would refuse it.
skeptic_correction: Reachability is stronger than the auditor stated. Every 'Reconstruir' with replace OFF on a completed session re-launches the fork (see missed item vggt_long.py:3877), and the fork then replays these files.

title: Scale and orientation markers are idempotent on existence only; pose backups are never refreshed
mechanism: run() returns the previous s, and orient.run() returns identity, whenever .metric_scale_applied / .orientation_applied exist. They do not check that the camera_poses.txt and chunk PLYs on disk are the ones that were transformed. Example: a resume after a crash between scale_align and cleanup re-copies unscaled pcd/*_pcd.ply over the scaled chunk_*.ply, while maplong_run/camera_poses.txt was already scaled and oriented. Cloud and poses then de-sync and are never re-scaled. The .prescale/.preorient backups are written only `if not bak.exists()`, so a backup from an earlier run of the same plan persists. precision/epoch0_cloud reads camera_poses.txt.prescale.
evidence: scale_align.py: `if marker.exists() and not dry_run: ... return s_prev`. orient.py:258: `if marker.exists(): ... return np.eye(4)`. Backups: `if not bak.exists(): shutil.copy(pp, bak)`.
fix_idea_auditor: Store in the marker the sha of the files it transformed. On reuse, verify those shas or redo from the raw poses. Overwrite the backups on every fresh fork pass.
skeptic_reason: The markers really are existence-only (scale_align.py:510-519, orient.py:256-260) and are not stamped. The auditor's scenario, however, is impossible. _postprocess_reconstruction deletes maplong_run/pcd in its cascade cleanup step 1/3 (map_worker.py:2939 → _cleanup_recon_temps), and that runs BEFORE scale_align, so unscaled pcd PLYs can never be re-copied over scaled chunk_*.ply after the marker is written. The .prescale backup is read only by precision/epoch0_cloud._read_prescale_and_epoch0, which is not in the omega_bent chain, because f6_bend imports only SKY_CONF and _write_ply_xyzrgb.
skeptic_correction: Real trigger: after a completed run, _discard_previous_epochs (map_worker.py:520) deletes output/chunk_*.ply and the cleanup deletes maplong_run/pcd. On the next replace-OFF Reconstruir, the fork's completion test fails and it re-runs. It rewrites maplong_run/camera_poses.txt and the chunk PLYs in Omega's raw frame. Then .metric_scale_applied (s=0.984577) and .orientation_applied (165.48°, ty 1.6856) are still present, so scale_align and orient both skip. The new poses and cloud are left unscaled and unoriented. The downstream effect on F0–F6 resume records was not verified.

title: Seeded subsampling over data-dependent index sets turns a one-pixel difference upstream into a fully re-drawn sample
mechanism: Every robust fit samples with default_rng(0).choice(len(valid), k) or a stride of max(1, size//k). Examples: robust_rigid/robust_sim3 (200k), exact_correspondences (per_frame_cap), surface_pair_correspondences/depth_pair_samples (8000), split_half_residual's permutation, chunk_covis.measured_tol's stride. The valid set comes from conf > 1e-5, isfinite and depth thresholds. If one pixel crosses a threshold, len changes and the RNG returns an unrelated subset. This is not a randomness source by itself, but it turns any ulp-level difference (card, kernel, resumed npy, sky-mask cache) into mm-level changes in seam R/t, bridge σ, held-out residuals and tol_rel. Those changes can flip the knife-edges in omega-01/02/15/17.
evidence: metric_lock.py:462 `idx = np.random.default_rng(seed).choice(len(src), sample, replace=False)`. loop_bridges.py:138 `idx = rng.choice(idx, int(per_frame_cap), replace=False)`. chunk_covis.py:186 `pool.append(r[:: max(1, r.size // 4000)])`.
fix_idea_auditor: Choose samples by a stable per-pixel key, for example keep pixel (frame, row, col) iff hash(frame, row, col) mod M < k·M/N_frame. Membership then does not reshuffle when one pixel enters or leaves the valid set.
skeptic_reason: Verified: metric_lock.py:461-462 default_rng(seed).choice(len(src)), loop_bridges.py:130-138, and chunk_covis.py:186 stride r.size//4000. These are seeded and deterministic for identical inputs. They are not a SOURCE of nondeterminism; they amplify an upstream bit difference into a re-drawn sample. Both runs logged identical values to 8 decimals up to the pose graph.
skeptic_correction: This is a sensitivity amplifier, not nondeterminism. Identical inputs give identical bits.

title: Numerics depend on the card: bf16/fp16 by compute capability, TF32 convolutions by default, kernel choice per GPU, solver device cuda-or-cpu
mechanism: The fork picks bf16 if capability ≥ 8 else fp16. VGGTOmega.forward picks amp_dtype via is_bf16_supported(). The dense head runs with autocast disabled in fp32, but torch.backends.cudnn.allow_tf32 is left at its default True, so its convolutions are TF32 on Ampere. SDPA/cuBLAS kernel selection varies by GPU model. The pose graph runs on 'cuda if available else cpu' (line 3010), giving different float64 last bits and possibly different LM accept/stop. Each is deterministic on one card, but products validated on another card are not bit-reproducible. CLAUDE.md names an RTX A6000 48 GB; both runs here ran on an A100 80GB PCIe.
evidence: vggt_long.py:137 `self.dtype = torch.bfloat16 if torch.cuda.get_device_capability()[0] >= 8 else torch.float16`. vggt_omega.py:39 `amp_dtype = torch.bfloat16 if torch.cuda.is_bf16_supported() else torch.float16`. vggt_long.py:3010 `_dev = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"`. No allow_tf32 setting anywhere in the fork.
fix_idea_auditor: Set cudnn.allow_tf32 and cuda.matmul.allow_tf32 to False explicitly. Fix the dtype in config. Fail rather than fall back to CPU for the graph. Record GPU model, driver, torch and cuDNN versions in chunk_plan.json and the fork outputs.
skeptic_reason: vggt_long.py:137 picks the dtype by compute capability, and 3010 picks the solver device. The fork sets no allow_tf32 (the only hit is DINOv2's train.py, not imported at inference). Each choice is fixed for one card, and both runs used the same A100, so this matters only across cards. The pose-graph assembly (pose_graph.py:315-346) is a sequential loop with dense Cholesky and no atomics.

title: A slow nvidia-smi turns the card name into 'unknown', which drops the learned footprint factor and invalidates the DA3 footprint cache
mechanism: card_name() runs nvidia-smi with timeout=20 and returns 'unknown' on timeout or error. map_worker then calls omega_footprint_factor('unknown') and gets 1.0 instead of 1.2139, which changes capacity and possibly resolution (see omega-03/14). The da3_vram.json key no longer matches, so the DA3 footprint is re-measured (omega-05 margin). nvidia-smi can stall while the GPU is busy.
evidence: Code: `out = subprocess.run(["nvidia-smi", "--query-gpu=name,memory.total", ...], timeout=20)` with `except (OSError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired): return "unknown"`.
fix_idea_auditor: Read the card identity in-process (torch.cuda.get_device_name + total_memory), or fail hard on timeout instead of returning a sentinel that changes decisions.
skeptic_reason: vram.py:81-87 returns 'unknown' on a non-zero exit, OSError or timeout. map_worker.py:2312-2313 then reads factor 1.0. The DA3 footprint key misses and the footprint is re-measured; on the same stack that re-measurement reproduced 11.09, so the window does not change. The Omega effect only matters near a capacity edge (omega-14).

title: Omega resolution comes from an integer capacity floor, recomputed every run with no hysteresis
mechanism: omega_capacity() = int((total·(1−margin) − 4)/per_frame), and the highest patch-aligned resolution with n_max ≤ capacity wins. Near the boundary, a small change in factor (omega-03), margin, card total or largest-chunk length moves the resolution by 16 px. That changes Omega's grid, depth, poses, F0's camera grid and every later stage. pccr is far from the edge (139 vs 613); zaragoza is not.
evidence: zaragoza (good-run log line 1223): 'the largest chunk (183 frames) does not fit at 1920; 1664 (grid 1664x928, capacity 186) is the largest ... (1680: grid 1680x944, capacity 181)'. That is a 3-frame margin.
fix_idea_auditor: Persist the resolution chosen for a session and reuse it unless the plan changes. Log the margin, and require explicit approval to change a session's resolution.
skeptic_reason: chunk_plan.py:134-139 takes an int() floor of capacity, and omega_resolution_for (209-230) chooses the first patch-aligned resolution with n <= capacity, with no hysteresis and nothing persisted per session.
skeptic_correction: The bad run is the sharpest case: zaragoza at 1520 has capacity 183 for a 183-frame chunk, a margin of zero frames. Any change to the factor or margin moves it one patch step. pccr is far from the edge.

title: Chunk ranges come from integer co-visibility lengths (majority of c >= 0.3 tests) and DP thresholds with about 1 % margin
mechanism: ℓ(i) counts passes of `c >= TAU` until fails > passes. δ = 1/ℓ, so one flipped test changes δ by 1/ℓ − 1/(ℓ±1). The exact DP accepts blocks with D ≤ H/2 = 6.835, then fewest blocks, worst seam z̄, worst cut θ, a tightest budget and leftmost tie-break. On pccr the chosen block budget is 6.769, about 1 % under the bound. A small δ change can move a cut or the block count, which changes Model.chunk_ranges and so all of Omega. Inputs are the I3 windows, so this flips only if those bits change (omega-05/06/12), but nothing records the margin.
evidence: Bad-run log: 'optimum: 6 blocks, worst seam z̄ 1.3379607200622559, worst cut 3.1878214834580207°, block budget 6.769288107832995'. H/2 = 6.835. Code: `if c >= TAU: passes += 1; last = b` ... `if fails > passes: ... break`.
fix_idea_auditor: Report the smallest margin of every constraint (each ℓ's closest c to TAU, D vs H/2) in covis.json. Freeze the plan per session (it is stamped already) and refuse silent re-planning when inputs change only at noise level.
skeptic_reason: chunk_covis.py:218-236 counts integer co-visibility lengths with the 'c >= TAU' rule and a majority stop. The plan is cached in covis.json under an input stamp (sha of windows.json and walk.json, chunk_covis.py:640-651), and both runs logged the same stamp. It flips only if the I3 window bits change.

title: Which candidates become bridges depends on hard bars on measured floats; the edge count then feeds the judge split
mechanism: Rule 0 rejects a candidate when the provisional chain's walked length L < min_walk_m (1.0 m). The SALAD bar is argmax of Youden's J over the session's unique similarities (calibration.py:40), applied with a strict `similarity <= threshold`, plus top-5 argsort and NMS. A candidate at L ≈ 1.0 m or similarity ≈ 0.416 flips on noise. That changes the number of bridges and verified edges, and so k and the judge count (omega-02).
evidence: Bad-run log: '[loop-gate] candidate 49<->29 (salad): REJECTED ... only 0.7 m walked (< 1.0 m)'. '[loops] SALAD bar CALIBRATED on 1102 geometric revisit pair(s): 0.416'. Code: `walk_ok = L >= min_walk`.
fix_idea_auditor: Log each candidate's margin to every bar. Keep the calibrated threshold as a persisted, stamped session value rather than re-deriving it on every run.
skeptic_reason: spatial_gate.py:330-331 has 'walk_ok = L >= min_walk'. LoopModels/calibration.py:40 uses argmax of Youden's J. Margins on pccr are wide (the rejected pair is at 0.73 m against 1.0 m). Note that the SALAD non-local band computed from the walk (ceil 16.5 → 17) does not decide anything on pccr, because the bridge-window floor of 20 dominates (log line 334).

title: The scale-break test multiplies a loop edge's σ (and its scale row's σ) by a factor on a strict threshold
mechanism: verify_loop: scale_ok = |log s_ab| <= scale_tol_log. Beyond it, status becomes scale_break and σ is multiplied by scale_break_sigma_factor. vggt_long.py:2296 applies the same test to the loop rows of the scale graph, which changes the solved δ per chunk. A bridge whose |log s_ab| sits at the tolerance changes chunk scales and the pose-edge weight.
evidence: Bad-run log: three '[scale-graph] SCALE BREAK on loop [4, 0]/[4, 3] ...' lines, then '7 loop row(s) ... max |δ| 1.44%'. Code: `scale_ok = abs(log_s) <= tol_log` and `is_break = abs(log_r_meas) > tol_log`.
fix_idea_auditor: Inflate σ continuously with |log s_ab|/tol instead of a step, or log the margin.
skeptic_reason: loop_bridges.py:385-386 'scale_ok = abs(log_s) <= tol_log' and vggt_long.py:2296-2298 'is_break = abs(log_r_meas) > tol_log' are step inflations of σ. Both are deterministic for identical inputs.

title: Zoom exclusion (robust z > 3.5) and the scale-drift gate (0.75 ratio) switch per-chunk scales by tens of %
mechanism: A chunk whose median fx has robust z > 3.5 loses its DA3 anchors and takes its scale from the seams. The scale-drift ramp applies when med_drift <= 0.75·med_const (metric_lock.py:411). Both are hard bars on measured floats. Flipping either changes chunk scale and so all metric geometry.
evidence: Bad-run log: 'chunk 3: optical ZOOM (fx 379 vs session 363, z=5.7) — DA3 anchors EXCLUDED', 'chunk 3: OPTIMAL s=2.2346 (no anchors — from seams)' against DA3's 1.8518. 'scale drift SKIPPED ... held-out 1.11% → 0.95%' (ratio 0.856 vs 0.75). Margins are wide on pccr.
fix_idea_auditor: Record each gate's margin in metric_lock.json. Weight anchors continuously by z instead of excluding them at a cut.
skeptic_reason: vggt_long.py:566-575 excludes a chunk at robust z > 3.5, computed from a MAD over only 5 chunk fx values. metric_lock.py:410 'ok = med_d <= improve·med_c'. Both are hard bars, but the margins on pccr are wide (z=5.7; ratio 0.856 against 0.75). The zoom decision changes chunk 3's scale by about 20 % (2.2346 vs 1.8518), so the effect is large even though a flip is unlikely.

title: Depth-graph rungs are judged by the same effect-size-free bootstrap; only the 'bounded' bar stops a re-depthing
mechanism: depth_graph_verdict uses heldout_change over about 486 held-out pairs, where any consistent shift gives improves=True. Applying a rung (per-frame z' = a z + b along the rays) requires bounded AND improves. Today bounded is False by a wide margin, so the improves flag decides nothing. If the scene satisfied bounded, the same issue as omega-01 would decide a per-frame depth warp.
evidence: Both runs: 'affine: held-out 0.64% -> 0.25/0.26% ... bounded=False improves=True', 'scale-only ... bounded=False improves=True', '⛔ no rung ... geometry left UNTOUCHED'.
fix_idea_auditor: Same as omega-01: require a declared minimum effect alongside the CI.
skeptic_reason: The depth-graph rungs need bounded AND improves. In both runs bounded=False by a wide margin (a in [0.70, 1.56], b up to 92 cm), so geometry was left untouched (log lines 506-508). Today the effect-size-free test decides nothing here.

title: Sky masks are cached by frame basename across runs and plans; skyseg.onnx is fetched from an unpinned HF 'main'
mechanism: sky_masks/<frame>.png is reused whenever it exists and survives new chunk plans (_PLAN_INDEPENDENT_MAPLONG). The cache key has no skyseg model hash, no frame content hash and no threshold. If skyseg.onnx is missing it is downloaded from huggingface.co/.../resolve/main/skyseg.onnx with no revision pin. The masks zero world_points_conf, which feeds conf>1e-5 masks everywhere (and omega-11). Fresh and cached masks are both 0/255 uint8, so this is consistent today.
evidence: Code: `if os.path.exists(mask_fp): sky = cv2.imread(mask_fp, cv2.IMREAD_GRAYSCALE) else: ... segment_sky(p, self.skyseg_session, mask_fp)` and `download_file_from_url("https://huggingface.co/JianyuanWang/skyseg/resolve/main/skyseg.onnx", onnx_path)`.
fix_idea_auditor: Key the cache directory on sha(skyseg.onnx) and pin the download to a commit hash, or vendor the ONNX file with a checksum.
skeptic_reason: vggt_long.py:269-290: the cache is keyed by frame basename only, and the download is unpinned from HF 'main'. vendor/VGGT-Long/skyseg.onnx is already present (dated Jun 4), so no download happens. A freshly computed mask and a cached one are both 0/255 uint8 (visual_util.segment_sky:393-398). It is consistent today.

title: I3 windows, walk.json and covis.json are reused on stamps that leave out the DA3 and planner code versions
mechanism: run_da3_windows reuses window_*.npz whenever windows.json lists the same paths, process_res and model_id. walk.json/anchors are reused via walk_is_current. covis.json is reused when its stamp (COVIS_VERSION, TAU, quantile, samples, horizon, sha of windows.json and walk.json) matches. None of these includes the DA3 package/weights revision, extract_da3_depth.py, or the covis measurement code (covis_dir/keyframe_views/budget) beyond a manual COVIS_VERSION bump. A code change can therefore reuse an old plan while a fresh run plans differently.
evidence: Code: `if isinstance(old, dict) and old.get("version") == COVIS_VERSION and old.get("stamp") == stamp: ... return old, "reused"`. walk.py: `if old != spec: for p in wdir.glob("window_*.npz"): p.unlink()` (reuse otherwise).
fix_idea_auditor: Add the git hash of chunk_covis.py and intake/walk.py, plus the DA3 package version and weights sha, to every stamp.
skeptic_reason: walk.py:263-268 decides reuse by comparing the windows.json spec only. chunk_covis.py:649 checks COVIS_VERSION plus the input stamp. Neither includes the DA3 or planner code version.

title: scale_absolute_rows.json from a previous certification enters the next run's metric lock if present (dormant today)
mechanism: map_worker reads output/scale_absolute_rows.json, if present, into Model.metric_lock.absolute_rows. These are absolute per-chunk scale rows in the in-run scale graph. The file is written post-hoc by reconstruction.loops.structural from regulated dimensions and survives resumes of the same plan. It has no epoch or plan stamp. Dormant now because loops.structural.regulated_dims is [].
evidence: Code: `_abs_path = output_dir / "scale_absolute_rows.json"; if _abs_path.exists(): _abs_rows = list(json.loads(_abs_path.read_text()).get("rows", []))`. config.yaml:3579 `regulated_dims: []`.
fix_idea_auditor: Stamp the rows with the plan, chunk ranges and epoch they were measured on, and ignore them unless they match the run being planned.
skeptic_reason: map_worker.py:2161-2165 reads the file when it exists, with no stamp. It is dormant: regulated_dims is [] (config.yaml:3579), and its writer path (instance_loops.py:639 under certify iterations) is also skipped under certify.deliverable_only.
skeptic_correction: This affects nothing today.

title: The DA3 window size, and with it the F2 gauge rows, depends on the card's TOTAL memory
mechanism: window_size sizes the I3 window as floor((total*(1-margin)-w)/per_frame) with total read from nvidia-smi memory.total. The same session on a 48 GB A6000 (the card CLAUDE.md names) gets (40.8-6.36)/2.365 = 14 frames per window instead of 26 on the A100. That gives different DA3 windows, different per-window Huber gains, different row groups and LOO folds, so a different gauge model and s_k. It also changes walk.json and the covis inputs. chunk_covis.H_CALIBRATION_LAYOUT declares this card dependence for the covis H. Nothing declares or checks it for the F2 gauge, whose rows come from the same windows.

title: DA3 picks each window's reference view by argmin of a bf16 'balance score' and reorders the views
mechanism: For windows of 3 or more frames (THRESH_FOR_REF_SELECTION=3, vision_transformer.py:314), b_idx = balance_score.argmin over min-max normalised class-token metrics computed under bf16 autocast (api.py:126). The chosen view is moved first and given the reference camera token, so a near-tie that flips changes the whole window's inference: the depth used by the F2 rows, and the walk. It is deterministic on the same card and stack (A and B identical). It can flip across cards or software, where bf16 kernels round differently.

title: DA3 weights come from different HF caches depending on how the process was launched
mechanism: The backend exports HF_HOME=/workspace/hf_cache, which holds the complete snapshot b2359bdf from May 30. The pod environment, inherited by by-hand runs such as the 'python -m precision.runner' now running (pid 2759308), has HF_HOME=/workspace/.cache/huggingface/. There the DA3NESTED-GIANT-LARGE-1.1 snapshot dir is empty (blobs/0c9ba5b7...incomplete, 0 bytes, 10-06 06:31). extract_da3_depth.py:189 loads from_pretrained with no revision. So a by-hand F2 window regeneration resolves and downloads refs/main at that moment into a second cache, while the pipeline keeps the old one. Both refs point to b2359bdf today, but nothing ties the run to that revision.

title: DA3 window files are reused when present, keyed only by window index and the windows.json content
mechanism: run_windows skips every window whose window_{i:04d}.npz exists. intake.walk.run_da3_windows clears them only when windows.json (paths, process_res, model_id) differs. A run interrupted part-way and resumed later (pipeline resume or F2 regeneration) mixes windows produced earlier with windows produced now. Nothing in the window files or in windows.json records the card, dtype, torch/cuDNN version or weights revision, so windows from another stack can feed the walk and the gauge.

title: The fork's 'already complete' test is defeated by the pipeline's own cleanup, so every replace-OFF Reconstruir on a finished session re-runs Omega under stale state
mechanism: The fork skips only if maplong_run/camera_poses.txt exists AND clouds exist (pcd/*_pcd.ply or output/chunk_*.ply). After a completed precision run, _cleanup_recon_temps deletes pcd/ and _discard_previous_epochs (map_worker.py:520) deletes output/chunk_*.ply, so _clouds_done is always False. pipeline_manager runs the reconstruction stage whenever Reconstruir is requested (upstream_ran = recon_requested). The fork then re-infers Omega (the unaligned npys were deleted) and replays every chunk_indices-keyed resume file: pose_graph.json verdict and xi, depth_graph a,b, uncertainty.json, and metric_lock 'already locked'. It rewrites camera_poses.txt in Omega's raw frame. The existence-only markers .metric_scale_applied (s=0.984577) and .orientation_applied (165.48°, ty 1.6856) are still on disk, so scale_align and orient skip, and output poses and chunks are left unscaled and unoriented. A replace-OFF run therefore cannot reproduce a fresh run. The downstream F0–F6 resume behaviour on this path was not verified.

title: The OOM learner parses only 'Tried to allocate X GiB'; an allocation under 1 GiB (printed in MiB by torch) takes a different, unlearned step-down
mechanism: record_omega_oom returns None unless the failing allocation is printed in GiB (regex r'Tried to allocate ([0-9.]+) GiB'). Torch formats allocations under 1 GiB as MiB. In that case map_worker.py:2424-2425 does not store a factor and drops the ceiling by √(1−margin) ≈ 8 % (1664 → about 1520). A GiB-sized failure instead stores a permanent factor and steps down by a single 16 px patch. So the size of the allocation that happened to fail decides both the retry resolution and whether weights/omega_footprint.json is rewritten for every later session on that card.

title: Each rung is solved cold from F0's camera and the initial poses (not from the previous rung's solution), and nothing checks that a nested rung reaches its parent's cost
mechanism: `r = run_rung(name, w2c0, params0, wh, fit_g, X0, sig, cfg)` starts R1 and R2 from the same F0 camera and poses. R2 is a superset of R1 (R1 plus the lens), so its optimum can never cost more than R1's, but the code never warm-starts R2 from R1 or compares their final costs. In run B, R2 ended at Ceres cost 0.48528 px (R1 0.458938) and fit median 0.4776 px (R1 0.4767), and the judge still took it on a held-out change of 0.0005 px. The R1/R2 verdict, and with it the lens, fy/cx and F6's carry path, therefore follows the LM path of a cold start. Changes a DECISION with visible downstream effect.

title: If R3 is taken, the session publishes block 0's camera for every keyframe, while the poses were solved with a focal per block
mechanism: `new_cam = cam.with_params(best.params_by_block[0], ...)` together with apply_pose_epoch(best.w2c). camera.json, intrinsic.txt (camera_travels) and F6's K all use one camera, block 0's. R3 is tried on every run (the temporal test fired in A and B, p = 1/2001) and is accepted by the same significance-only judge as R2. In B its verdict was 'worsens' by 0.0008 px, CI entirely negative. If the sign of that practically-zero effect flipped, F5 would publish poses and a camera that do not belong together, and F6 would triangulate and unproject every block other than 0 with the wrong focal. Latent; a DECISION.

title: The epoch number written into every point and report depends on the session's epoch history, not on the inputs
mechanism: publish fills the origins.npz `geometry_epoch` column with `np.full(n, epoch_to, ...)`, where epoch_to = next_epoch(out). The cleaned PLY carries no such field, so this branch is the one taken. The same epoch_to goes into corrected_cloud.json, depth_on_f5.json and the epoch record, and F5 likewise bumps geometry_epoch and camera_epoch. After a different history (an undo, as the session now has epoch 4 = refine_undo of epoch 2, or an extra correction epoch), identical F5/F6 inputs therefore produce different bytes. Changes BITS only.

title: Poses travel between stages as text with 8 significant digits ('{:.8g}'): every pass through camera_poses.txt rounds them
mechanism: camera_poses.txt (and its copies) are written with '{:.8g}' (lossy) and re-read by every stage; observed 2026-10-07: undoing F5 by its exact inverse transform and re-running F5 from the 'same' F2 poses gave R0 residuals 6657045 vs 6657053, initial cost 3.2625 vs 3.2395 px, degenerate 640 vs 701, held-out 0.5447 vs 0.5492 px
